clue.text: Stewed kangaroo he set before master down under?

indicators.note: stewing breaks food down and mixes it up, so the following words are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder, every letter used once

explanation.surface: A cook stews a kangaroo and serves it before the master of the house in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Down under suggests Australia and the kangaroo, but this is a Maori phrase from New Zealand: a kohanga reo is a Maori-language preschool, a 'language nest'.
explanation.definitionFit: A preschool group is a class of children taught before they ever reach a schoolmaster, and the question mark flags the playful framing.

clue.text: Poisonous plant, one initially carried by river current

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the first letter of one
the Ural is a Russian river
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A toxic plant is swept along by the flow of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one thing carried by another sits on top of it, so the first letter comes above the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Ourali is another name for curare, the arrow poison, and for the South American vine it is made from.

clue.text: One to a bush, curiously large strawberry

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so the preceding letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that, oddly, a single bush has produced an enormous strawberry.
explanation.definitionFit: The hautbois, or hautboy, is a tall European strawberry plant bearing large musky fruit, named from French for high wood.

clue.text: Resisting wine Greek character's left

indicators.note: left means gone away, so the Greek letter departs from the wine's name

parts.note: Chianti is a Tuscan red wine
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person has walked out, refusing the wine on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being anti something means opposing or standing against it, an adjective sense that matches resisting.

clue.text: US never accepting prince with English serviettes?

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the American word for never holds the other letters

parts.note: nary is American dialect for never or not one
P is the abbreviation for prince
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An American refuses ever to let a prince use English napkins.
explanation.walkthrough: Serviette is the British word for a table napkin.
explanation.definitionFit: Napery is household table linen, which includes napkins; the question mark admits that serviettes are only one example.

clue.text: Once greeted distracted great-aunt — with never an answer

indicators.note: someone distracted has their thoughts in disarray, so these letters are jumbled
with never means not having any at all, so every instance is struck out

parts.note: taken as written, without the hyphen
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: An elderly relative was greeted by someone too preoccupied to give any reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Greet is Scots for weep, so greeted here means wept, not welcomed; both letters A go before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Grutten is an old Scots past participle of greet, to cry or weep, hence the once.

clue.text: Take back focus again during speech

indicators.note: during speech means as spoken, so we want a sound rather than a spelling

parts.note: to refocus a camera is to zoom it once more

explanation.surface: A speaker regains the thread and concentrates again while talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume can mean to reoccupy or reclaim something previously held, as when one resumes one's seat.

clue.text: Being new, note two hands get involved in problems

definitions.note: used intransitively; Chambers gives ensnarl as to entangle

parts.note: ens is the philosophers' word for a being or entity
N is the abbreviation for new
A is a musical note
R and L are right and left, the two hands

explanation.surface: A newcomer finds both hands busy as they become caught up in difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnarl is to entangle, as in a snare, so becoming tangled up in trouble fits the verb.

clue.text: Brazilian unit continued on

parts.note: cont. is the standard abbreviation of continued
o' is a dialect shortening of on, as in o' nights

explanation.surface: A report about a Brazilian military unit carries on.
explanation.definitionFit: A conto was a money of account in Brazil and Portugal worth a thousand milreis, so a monetary unit.

clue.text: Lobster trap let adrift went up to the vessel's bottom

parts.note: a lobster pot is a trap

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top
something adrift has come loose and wandered, so the word let is jumbled

parts.note: the fodder
slang for urinated

explanation.surface: A lobster pot breaks loose and rises from the bottom of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A pottle is an old two-quart drinking vessel; Shakespeare's Iago speaks of drinking pottle-deep.
explanation.definitionFit: Pottle-deep means drunk right down to the bottom of the pottle, the old measure of ale or wine.

clue.text: Bird taking adult lizard

parts.note: a guan is a South American game bird
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A bird of prey seizes a full-grown lizard.
explanation.definitionFit: Guana is an older variant name for the iguana, the large tropical American reptile.

clue.text: Information also relating to language

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
a synonym

explanation.surface: Someone supplies linguistic facts as well.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a dry note on linguistics; it hides an old Anglo-Indian word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentoo was an old Anglo-Indian term for Hindu, and as an adjective was applied to the Telugu tongue.

clue.text: Medicinal plant banks caught dividing plantain

parts.note: asar is a plural of as, a glacial ridge or esker

indicators.note: dividing means splitting apart, so this goes inside and separates the plant name

parts.note: abaca is the Manila hemp plantain
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: On the riverbanks a herb has been found growing among the plantain.
explanation.definitionFit: Asarabacca, or wild ginger, is a European herb once used as an emetic and in snuff.

clue.text: As inputs for processing with power

indicators.note: material sent for processing is worked over and comes out reshaped

parts.note: the fodder, every letter used once

explanation.surface: Data inputs are fed into a powerful computer for processing.
explanation.definitionFit: Puissant is a literary adjective for powerful or mighty, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Surfeit of tasty cooking that is included

indicators.note: included means put inside, so the abbreviation goes within the other letters
cooking transforms the ingredients, so the word tasty is reworked

parts.note: the fodder
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A diner has had too much of delicious home cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiety is the state of being fully satisfied or glutted, an excess of gratification like a surfeit.

clue.text: Polled too much after end of campaign

indicators.note: end of picks out only the closing letter of the next word

parts.note: the final letter of campaign
OTT, over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: After an election campaign closes, someone complains there has been excessive opinion polling.
explanation.walkthrough: Polled looks like voting; here it means hornless or shorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Nott is an old word for hornless or close-cropped, the farming sense of polled cattle.

clue.text: Attachment to watch with right time on even if old

parts.note: albe is an archaic form of albeit, meaning although
R is the abbreviation for right
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A watch keeps correct time even though it is an antique.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, time on the other pieces means it follows them.
explanation.definitionFit: An albert is a short watch chain fastened to a waistcoat, named after Prince Albert, who wore one.

clue.text: What's regularly used in backing all-out war — mean explosive

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the kept letters are read right to left
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the even letters of these words

explanation.surface: In total war, a nasty explosive gets deployed again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Amatol is a high explosive mixing TNT with ammonium nitrate, widely used in shells and bombs in both world wars.

clue.text: Row in Scotland, weary about split

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for weary is wrapped round the other

parts.note: to tire is to weary
to rive is to split or tear apart

explanation.surface: A Scot, fed up with a breakup, has had enough of the quarrelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirrivee is a Scots word for a tantrum or commotion, a row in the sense of a noisy disturbance.

clue.text: Second old pound note turned up, put into stock collection?

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means flipped to read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
O is the abbreviation for old
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
me is the third note of the sol-fa scale, also spelt mi

explanation.surface: An old pound note surfaces a second time and is added to a coin collector's stock.
explanation.walkthrough: Stock here is the garden flower, not goods in store.
explanation.definitionFit: To embloom is to cover with flowers, so to plant out a bed of stocks would embloom it; the question mark marks the stretch.

clue.text: Rinse around in edges of eye, something helping vision

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the jumbled letters go within the others
edges of keeps only the outermost letters of the next word

parts.note: the first and last letters of eye

indicators.note: around suggests being moved about, so the word rinse is jumbled

parts.note: the fodder

explanation.surface: Bathing the eye helps clear one's sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Eserine, or physostigmine, is an alkaloid used in eye drops to contract the pupil and treat glaucoma.

clue.text: Stewed kangaroo — it is covered in pork fat, right?

indicators.note: something covered in a coating is wrapped inside it, so this goes within the fat

parts.note: seame is Shakespeare's spelling of seam, hog's lard
't is the old shortened form of it, as in 'tis
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a stewed kangaroo dish really comes smothered in pork dripping.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a second appearance of the stewed kangaroo from 1 across, now as a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer was an old Australian colonial dish of kangaroo meat stewed with pork, or a pan for cooking it.

clue.text: Insect eating what is sticky food

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so the insect swallows the other word

parts.note: an ant is an insect
birdlime, a sticky substance smeared on twigs to trap birds

explanation.surface: An insect dines on something gooey.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for nourishment or anything that feeds, related to alimentary.

clue.text: What changes bare centre of lobe?

definitions.text: What changes bare centre of lobe?

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: centre of keeps only the middle letters of the following word

parts.note: the two middle letters of lobe

explanation.surface: A riddle asks what transforms the naked middle of an ear.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An earbob is an earring, an ornament hung from the earlobe that changes how an unadorned ear looks.

clue.text: Layers of society to whatever extent restricting courtesan rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top
restricting means hemming in, so the first word holds the second

parts.note: as, as in as much as you can
tart is slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A courtesan climbs through society, however far it takes her.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are the levels or classes into which a society is divided, borrowed from geology.

clue.text: Rock outcrop regularly used for signals, I hear

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the even letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone has heard that a rocky crag is routinely used for signalling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' looks like a sound-alike signal; it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlier is an area of older rock entirely surrounded by younger strata, exposed at the surface.

clue.text: Ban on business line for sharing power

parts.note: bus. is the abbreviation for business
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A company bans sharing a power line.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, one word on another comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A busbar is a metal conductor that distributes electric current to several circuits in a switchboard or substation.

clue.text: Diver forbidden to come up without oxygen

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means reading from the bottom upwards
without here means outside, so the other letters wrap around the element

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A scuba diver is not allowed to surface without an air supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking; here it means outside, its old sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat is a German submarine, a vessel that dives beneath the surface.

clue.text: What was everlasting base metal alloy

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
terne is an alloy of lead and tin

explanation.surface: A cheap metal alloy that used to last forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base metal' reads as a single phrase, but base stands alone here.
explanation.definitionFit: Eterne is an archaic poetic form of eternal, hence the What was, signalling an obsolete word.

clue.text: Murder victim, the first to be pushed off tower?

indicators.text: the first to be pushed off
indicators.note: the opening letter is shoved away, so the word loses its start

parts.note: the Tower of Babel in Genesis

explanation.surface: A murder in which the first victim was thrown from a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are biblical: Babel from Genesis 11 and its victim from Genesis 4.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel, son of Adam and Eve, was killed by his brother Cain, the first murder in the Bible.

clue.text: Pipe river round barrage regularly

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the river goes around the other letters

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river

indicators.note: regularly means at steady intervals, so alternate letters are taken

parts.note: the even letters of barrage

explanation.surface: A river's flow is piped around a dam at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: A barrage is also a dam, which makes the river picture convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nargile is an oriental tobacco pipe that draws smoke through water, a hookah.

clue.text: Good bird cry heard in the Highlands?

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A fine bird's call rings out over the Scottish mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The Highlands are the mountainous north of Scotland, so the definition flags a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gowl is Scots for a howl or yell, so a loud cry in Scottish usage.

clue.text: What might stop one seeing wolf in unconscious state

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the animal sits within the other word

parts.note: a coma is a state of deep unconsciousness
lobo is the Spanish name for a timber wolf of the American West

explanation.surface: Someone in a coma cannot see a wolf at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloboma is a congenital gap in part of the eye, such as the iris or retina, which can impair sight.

clue.text: California's leading house to back old US company

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
ho. is the abbreviation for house

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the word to is read right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Californian house leads the backing for an old American firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Cahoot, now mostly in 'in cahoots', was once American slang for a partnership or league.

clue.text: Kilt finally bearing Scots fabric

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of kilt
in heraldry a weel is a charge, and a charge is called a bearing

explanation.surface: A kilt displays the cloth of a Scottish tartan.
explanation.walkthrough: Bearing is the heraldic word for a figure on a coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweel is the Scots form of twill, a cloth woven with diagonal ribs.

clue.text: Warning right after beer of a sort

parts.note: amber ale is a style of beer
rt is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone issues a warning after drinking some kind of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, right after the beer means it follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An amber alert is a warning of moderate danger, or the public bulletin broadcast when a child is abducted.
